title: Release audit: --uninstall omits ~/.bashrc, although the previous installer wrote the marked bl
summary: Include ~/.bashrc in the legacy cleanup set for uninstall, update the README list, and extend CANDIDATE_PROFILES/test_uninstall_clears_every_candidate_profile to cover it.
requirements: The uninstall path of install.sh must treat ~/.bashrc as a file that can contain the installer's marked block, in addition to the files it already handles.

The set of files the uninstall path cleans must be a superset of the set of files the install path can write the marked block to for bash, i.e. both the ~/.bash_profile branch and the ~/.bashrc branch.
Uninstall must remove the block delimited by the installer's existing begin/end marker lines, and must leave every other line of the file unchanged in content and order.
Uninstall must not fail, and must not modify a file, when a candidate startup file is missing, unreadable or contains no marked block.
Running uninstall twice must produce the same result as running it once: the second run finds no marked block and leaves the files unchanged.
The fix must not change the install path's behaviour: a fresh install still writes exactly one marked block into the same file it selected before.

tests/test_install.py must contain a regression test whose name contains `bashrc`; it sets up a temporary HOME with a ~/.bashrc containing the marked block written by the install path (no ~/.bash_profile present, or ~/.bashrc present), runs the uninstall, and asserts the block is gone and unrelated lines survive.

tests/test_install.py must contain an idempotence test whose name contains `idempotent`; it runs uninstall twice against the same temporary HOME and asserts the file is unchanged between the two runs and free of markers.
All tests must operate on a temporary HOME (or equivalent environment override already used by the suite) and must never read or write the invoking user's real startup files.
install.sh must remain syntactically valid POSIX sh compatible with the interpreter it already declares.
acceptance: After a simulated install for a bash home whose selected target is ~/.bashrc, running `install.sh --uninstall` leaves ~/.bashrc without the marked block and without any leftover marker line.
Unrelated lines in the cleaned startup file are preserved byte-for-byte (verified by comparing the file against a fixture with only the block removed).
A second `--uninstall` run leaves every candidate startup file unchanged.
A missing or block-free candidate startup file does not make uninstall fail (exit status remains the script's normal success status).
The full existing test suite passes.
install.sh passes a shell syntax check.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

result.summary: Fixed the release-audit defect whereby `install.sh --uninstall` ignored `~/.bashrc`. `PROFILE_NAMES` in install.sh now includes `.bashrc`, so the uninstall path strips the installer's marked PATH block from `~/.bashrc` in addition to the files it already cleaned (`.zshrc`, `.zprofile`, `.zshenv`, `.bash_profile`, `.bash_login`, `.profile`), while the install path, marker text and CLI stay unchanged. The existing tolerant/byte-preserving `remove_profile_block` path is reused, so missing or marker-free files are no-ops and repeated runs do not modify anything. In tests/test_install.py the uninstall candidate list gained `.bashrc`, a `_marked_block` helper builds the exact install block, `test_uninstall_removes_the_marked_block_from_bashrc` covers the bash/`~/.bashrc` regression (block gone, `# keep-before`/`export EDITOR=vi`/`# keep-after` preserved), and `test_repeated_uninstall_of_bashrc_is_idempotent` runs `--uninstall` twice over all candidate files and asserts each file is unchanged the second time and free of markers. All work runs against a temporary HOME. Tested with `python -m pytest -q tests/test_install.py -k 'bashrc or idempotent'` (3 passed) and the full suite `python -m pytest -q` (180 passed, 137 subtests), which also runs `sh -n install.sh`.
assumptions: The uninstall candidate list, not the install selection logic, was the defect; the install path was left untouched.

The regression and idempotence tests write the marked block directly (via a `_marked_block` helper matching the installer's block format) instead of running a full offline pip install, because the current install path selects `~/.bash_profile`/`.profile` for bash and never `~/.bashrc`; this reproduces the upgrade-leftover state described by the audit while keeping the tests fast and hermetic.
`.bashrc` was appended to the test module's `CANDIDATE_PROFILES` so the pre-existing every-candidate-profile test also covers it.

review.summary: The change is minimal and targeted: `PROFILE_NAMES` in install.sh gains `.bashrc`, and since that variable is consumed only by `uninstall`, the uninstall path now strips the marked block from `~/.bashrc` while the install path, marker text and CLI surface are untouched. `remove_profile_block` already tolerates missing, unreadable and block-free files and is idempotent, so FR-3/FR-4/FR-5 hold for the new candidate without extra logic. tests/test_install.py adds a `bashrc` regression test with an exact byte-for-byte expectation, adds an `idempotent` double-uninstall test over every candidate profile, extends `CANDIDATE_PROFILES`, and factors the block text into a `_marked_block` helper whose output matches the installer's block byte for byte; the pre-existing string-concatenation refactors keep the same content. All tests use a temporary HOME and no test was deleted or weakened. One cosmetic nit: `assertNotIn("Removed the PATH block", second.stdout)` is vacuous because the script never prints that phrase, but it does not affect the requirement. Minor note: the bashrc test writes the block in the exact install format rather than invoking the installer (whose bash branch cannot select `~/.bashrc`, since a fresh bash install verifies through `-l -i`), which is the only feasible way to reproduce the audited state and matches the spec's fixture allowance.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: uninstall treats ~/.bashrc as a file that can contain the marked block
FR-2: uninstall file set is a superset of the bash install targets (`.bash_profile` branch and `.bashrc`)
requirements.note: List covers .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile plus .bashrc; a custom FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE is still cleaned as before.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: block between existing markers removed, all other lines unchanged in content and order
requirements.note:
Unchanged awk-based `remove_profile_block`; the bashrc test compares the full file against `# keep-before
export EDITOR=vi
# keep-after
`.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: missing/unreadable/block-free candidate does not fail or modify the file
requirements.note: `remove_profile_block` returns 0 for non-files and for files without MARKER_START; idempotence test exercises block-free reruns.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: second uninstall produces the same result as the first
requirements.note: `test_repeated_uninstall_of_bashrc_is_idempotent` snapshots all candidate files after run one and compares after run two.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: install path behaviour unchanged (one block in the same selected file)
requirements.note: Only the uninstall-only `PROFILE_NAMES` list changed; `profile_path`, markers and block-writing code are untouched.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: regression test with `bashrc` in its name, temp HOME, block in ~/.bashrc, no ~/.bash_profile, asserts block gone and unrelated lines survive
requirements.note: `test_uninstall_removes_the_marked_block_from_bashrc` does all of this; it writes the block in the installer's exact byte format via `_marked_block` rather than running the installer, which matches the spec's fixture allowance and is the only reproducible state since the install path's bash branch never selects ~/.bashrc.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: idempotence test with `idempotent` in its name, two uninstall runs, unchanged file, no markers
requirements.note: `test_repeated_uninstall_of_bashrc_is_idempotent` verifies both runs and marker counts; the `assertNotIn("Removed the PATH block", ...)` line is vacuous but harmless.

requirements.note: `InstallerCase` uses `tempfile.mkdtemp` and `HOME`/`FORGEL_CODE_*` overrides; no real home path is read or written.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: install.sh remains valid POSIX sh
requirements.note: Change is a string literal only; QA ran `sh -n install.sh` (pass).
